record_identity.title: Zillow exited Zillow Offers after home-price forecasting produced excessive business volatility

incident_identity.date_basis: Date follows the reviewed registry or primary occurrence record; no narrower time is inferred.

summary: Zillow announced the wind-down of Zillow Offers after concluding that unpredictability in forecasting home prices was greater than anticipated and that continued scaling would create excessive earnings and balance-sheet volatility. AI Incident Database records the occurrence as involving Zillow's machine-learning-assisted Zestimate and the shutdown included a reduction of approximately 25% of Zillow's workforce.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Zillow announced the wind-down of Zillow Offers after concluding that unpredictability in forecasting home prices was greater than anticipated and that continued scaling would create excessive earnings and balance-sheet volatility. AI Incident Database records the occurrence as involving Zillow's machine-learning-assisted Zestimate and the shutdown included a reduction of approximately 25% of Zillow's workforce.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Zillow tied a capital-intensive home-buying operation to forecasts whose error and volatility proved harder to manage at scale than anticipated. The evidence supports a governance problem at the boundary between predictive uncertainty and business commitment, but it does not show that one model alone caused the shutdown.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: When forecasts drive purchases, inventory and balance-sheet exposure, uncertainty must constrain the scale and reversibility of the decisions built on them. Monitoring average model performance is insufficient if correlated forecast error can accumulate across a large portfolio before the organisation can exit safely.
assessment_boundaries: Zillow's announcement attributes the wind-down to greater-than-expected home-price forecasting unpredictability and resulting financial volatility, not to one isolated technical defect.
The record does not attribute all business losses or the workforce reduction solely to the Zestimate model.
Individual livelihood effects beyond the reported workforce reduction are not inferred.
The assessment does not reconstruct Zillow's private models, thresholds or acquisition decisions.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 classifies the occurrence under VIGIL-FC-000062 Epistemic Reliance Miscalibration at medium confidence. The preserved record ties Zillow Offers to machine-learning-assisted home-price forecasting and records Zillow's conclusion that forecasting unpredictability was greater than anticipated and that continued scaling created excessive earnings and balance-sheet volatility. Predictive price estimates were therefore incorporated into a capital-intensive home-acquisition workflow at an assurance level that proved insufficient for the consequential reliance condition of the business process. Confidence is medium because the public record does not reconstruct Zillow's private models, decision thresholds, human review, portfolio controls or the proportion of losses attributable to any one predictive system. VIGIL-FC-000046 Inferential Evidence–Authority Conflation is not used because the evidence does not show a prediction being treated as independent authority in place of a separately required entitlement or decision basis; the better fit is reliability/uncertainty miscalibration in a reliance-bearing workflow.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Machine-learning-assisted home-price forecasts were incorporated into a capital-intensive acquisition workflow whose consequential financial reliance required stronger calibration and uncertainty handling than the realised forecasting performance supported; Zillow later cited greater-than-anticipated forecast unpredictability and excessive balance-sheet volatility in winding the business down.

Accepted mappings: VIGIL-FC-000062. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000046: the record does not establish that a predictive state independently conferred authority for a decision beyond a separately required authority basis; the evidenced problem is use of predictive estimates at insufficient assurance for the scale of financial reliance. External-assessment material was checked where present or materially attributable in preserved sources; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Newly classified under taxonomy 0.6.5: FC-000062 primary, failure-occurrence, medium confidence.
